recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-39034 unless a later work-group decision changes Subscription notification parameter semantics.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive R5 issue asking to replace Subscription.header, a repeatable string collection, with Subscription.parameter 0..* as a BackboneElement with required string name and value children, allowing repeated names with channel-specific interpretation.
initial_application: Applied by c7ec1674c87447bafbfc174e4c9f1902670c49c4, which replaced Subscription.header with Subscription.parameter in the StructureDefinition, updated the REST hook narrative, and converted the admission example to parameter.name/parameter.value.
additional_context: Subscription is active in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-I WGM 202301 minutes confirm an 11-0-0 agreement that implementations would benefit from key-value pairs. A later Zulip subscriptions thread from the assignee described the header-to-parameter change as intended to support more complicated authorization flows. Later Subscription source edits preserved the parameter model, and searches found no conflicting final issue for this exact replacement.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active StructureDefinition defines Subscription.parameter 0..* as a BackboneElement with name and value child strings, notes that duplicate names are allowed subject to channel restrictions, and the narrative/example source consistently maps parameters to HTTP headers for REST hook subscriptions.
